name: Eve
source_summary: The first woman, formed by God from Adam's rib to be his companion; deceived by the serpent into eating the forbidden fruit, she shares in humanity's fall into sin but also receives the first promise of a deliverer who would one day crush the serpent.
family_friendly_summary: Eve was the first woman God ever made. God formed her from a rib taken from Adam, so she would have a companion just like him. Adam and Eve lived together in the beautiful garden of Eden, caring for it and enjoying friendship with God. But a clever serpent lied to Eve, telling her that eating fruit from the one tree God said not to touch would make her wise like God. Eve believed the lie, ate the fruit, and gave some to Adam, who ate it too. This first sin brought sadness and hardship into the world. But right after, God made a promise: that one day, someone from Eve's own family line would defeat the serpent for good -- a promise that points forward to Jesus. Eve became "the mother of all the living," and later she and Adam had more children, including Seth, and kept trusting God.
adult_story: Eve is formed by God from Adam's rib after none of the animals proves to be a companion "corresponding to" Adam (Genesis 2:18-23); Adam names her "Woman" and later "Eve," "because she was the mother of all the living" (3:20). She and Adam are together commanded not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, and it is Eve the serpent approaches, twisting God's word ("Indeed, has God said...?") until she believes the fruit is "good for food... a delight to the eyes, and... desirable to make one wise" (3:1-6). She eats, gives some to Adam, who eats without objection, and the couple's eyes are opened -- not to wisdom, but to shame (3:7). When God confronts her, Eve names the deception honestly: "The serpent deceived me, and I ate" (3:13); Paul later notes specifically that Eve, not Adam, was deceived, while Adam sinned with full knowledge (1 Timothy 2:14) -- Scripture assigns the two of them different, not lesser, culpability. God's judgment on the serpent includes the first gospel promise in Scripture: Eve's offspring will one day crush the serpent's head, at the cost of being struck himself (3:15) -- a promise that looks forward to Christ. Eve is driven with Adam from Eden, bears Cain, Abel, and later Seth, and calls Cain's birth a gift "with the help of the LORD" (4:1) -- even after the fall, still trusting God for life.
devotionals: The serpent twisted God's word until Eve believed disobedience would make her wise, but even as God judged her, He promised her offspring would one day crush the serpent's head. That first gospel promise finds its answer in Jesus, who crushed sin and death though it cost Him everything.

After losing Eden, Eve still called her son 'a gift with the help of the LORD,' trusting God even in the wreckage the fall had caused. We can trust God the same way after our own failures, since Jesus has already secured our future no less certainly than He promised hers.
